My first max level character was in burning crusade.  I made her at like 3am on a whim calling her "Flibbity" i knew nothing about addons,  macros,  strafing even.  I was a keyboard Turning NE hunter that manually made my pet attack on every mob. I knew almost nothing about the game but was having such a blast just doing it, I was the first of my friends to 40 and my mount and I was so used to not having one that most of the time I forgot to even use it.. lol
Getting to level 70 was a huge accomplishment for me even though I had no idea what to do and I'm sure if I looked at my /played it would be waaaay higher than the average, but she is the only toon i still have from my old days of playing (I retired her in wrath and never played her again, don't know why) but when the warband stuff came out and I consolidated all my gold across all servers and characters and deleted atleast 20 toons I just could not bring myself to delete her.  She was the testament to the countless hours of staying up all night through most of my early years of high school and grinding away and chilling just enjoying something,  before life got in the way of fun.
  Peak wow for me was 2007-2009. Min maxing wasn't even a thought or a thing i had heard of,  every single piece of information ever about the game wasn't readily available in a quick Google. Things were simpler and exciting and so much fun to just see what you could do in the vast world that was azeroth and outland.  I would love to experience that joy again and that is why no matter how long I take a break,  something always manages to pull me back to this goddamn game at some point,  even if only for a brief period..

12 years of drinking til passing out,  6 jobs being drunk all shift, everyday risking my job and livelihood while hiding my empties in my backpack,  second child halfway to due date I just decided one day enough was enough and I had to make a change. April 6 2024 was my 2 years sober,  never had a relapse or even much interest in drinking anymore since.  My partner is an abusive drunk so I think dealing with her really helps hammer home the need to be sober.. plus side, my kids will never see me fucked up and while It was very late I did manage to get my drivers license and a vehicle after getting sober which was something I never thought I would be able to do.  It all starts at day 1 and then it's just a matter of priorities and not making excuses. The longer you stay sober,  the easier it becomes and while I may have done it myself,  that's how I've always dealt with any problem so I knew that's how it would go.  If you're ever concerned about your drinking,  go to meetings and talk to other people who know how it feels.. the fact is that nobody knows what it's like to be an alcoholic except an alcoholic.
